clue.text: Hence aim diverted (for heretic)

indicators.note: diverted means turned from its course, so the letters of hence and aim are sent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone, aim thrown off, is led astray into heresy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' rearranges HENCEAIM. A Manichee follows Mani's dualist faith, branded heresy by the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Manichaeism, the dualist creed of light and darkness, was condemned by the Church as a heretic.

clue.text: Jellyfish, providing theme for Robert Nichols

definitions.meaning: the title and subject of a sonnet sequence by the war poet Robert Nichols

explanation.surface: A jellyfish inspires a poet's verses.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon jelly genus bears this name, and the poet Robert Nichols addressed a 1920 sonnet sequence to a woman so called.

clue.text: Batty one reported by Anne Rice

definitions.text: Batty one reported by Anne Rice

parts.words: Batty one reported by Anne Rice
parts.note: a batty one is a vampire, a bat-like creature, and Anne Rice's novel reports talking to one: the first word of her title is wanted

explanation.surface: An eccentric person is written up by a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne Rice's novel is Interview with the Vampire; 'batty' hints at a vampire turning into a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Rice's best-known novel takes the form of a vampire's recorded conversation with a reporter, and the title's first word names that exchange.

clue.text: Eminent convert of Waugh

parts.note: Evelyn Waugh wrote a novel about the Roman empress who became a Christian and found the True Cross

explanation.surface: A distinguished person converted by a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Waugh, himself a Catholic convert, titled his 1950 novel after the mother of Constantine.
explanation.definitionFit: Waugh's novel tells of the mother of Emperor Constantine, a famous early convert to Christianity and later a saint.

clue.text: She entered a small grey, and won the Carnegie Medal

definitions.text: She entered a small grey, and won the Carnegie Medal

parts.words: She entered a small grey, and won the Carnegie Medal
parts.note: a small grey suggests a pony at a show, but it points to the novelist's prize-winning book The Little White Horse

explanation.surface: A woman shows a little grey pony and takes a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: A white horse is called a grey; the English novelist's The Little White Horse won the 1946 Carnegie Medal for children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: The English novelist wrote The Little White Horse, a children's book awarded the Carnegie Medal in 1946.

clue.text: Boost, say, for kings of Spain and Macedon

definitions.note: plural in the clue because the name was borne by several kings, the answer being the single name

indicators.note: say signals that the word for boost is spoken, giving a name with the same sound

parts.note: a boost or stimulus is a fillip

explanation.surface: A boost given to royal rulers of two nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Several Spanish monarchs and the father of Alexander the Great, ruler of Macedon, bore this royal name.

clue.text: What we cannot speak about we must in silence" (Wittgenstein, Tractatus)

definitions.text: What we cannot speak about we must in silence" (Wittgenstein, Tractatus)

parts.words: What we cannot speak about we must in silence" (Wittgenstein, Tractatus)
parts.note: the closing proposition of Wittgenstein's Tractatus with a gap after must; the missing two words complete it

explanation.surface: The famous last line of Wittgenstein's Tractatus, with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: the answer fills the gap after 'must'. The Tractatus ends 'Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must pass over in silence'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase meaning to omit or leave unmentioned completes the quotation; written as one word it is also the Jewish spring festival.

clue.text: Alight in one cadence devised by blind composer

parts.note: to alight, as a bird or plane, is to land
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Something lands in a musical cadence invented by a sightless composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Francesco Landini was a blind fourteenth-century Florentine composer; the cadence associated with him carries his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The cadence with a decorated sixth before the final note is named after the blind Florentine composer Francesco Landini.

clue.text: Achilles was "weeping, cursing, VOWing vengeance for him

definitions.text: Achilles was "weeping, cursing, VOWing vengeance for him

parts.words: Achilles was "weeping, cursing, VOWing vengeance for him
parts.note: in the Iliad Achilles mourns and swears revenge on Hector for the death of his dearest companion

explanation.surface: A Greek hero mourns and swears revenge for a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Hector killed Achilles' friend, who had fought in Achilles' armour; Achilles' grief drives him back to battle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Iliad Achilles' beloved comrade is slain by Hector, and Achilles grieves and vows to avenge him.

clue.text: Greek telecast, featuring sound of grim child

annotationWithheld.why: Greek telecast, featuring sound of grim child (6): GRETEL is not hidden as one run in 'Greek telecast' and no parse of the printed words gives it; the clue looks misread or garbled
annotationWithheld.clue: Greek telecast, featuring sound of grim child

clue.text: "Coffee house wits — by me, can correct an author's style " (Swift, Battle of the Books)

definitions.text: "Coffee house wits — by me, can correct an author's style " (Swift, Battle of the Books)

parts.words: "Coffee house wits — by me, can correct an author's style " (Swift, Battle of the Books)
parts.note: a quotation from Swift with a gap marked by the dash; the missing word means innate prompting

explanation.surface: A quotation from Swift on coffee-house critics, with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: Swift's Criticism boasts that coffee-house wits, prompted by inborn feeling through her, can correct an author's style.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Swift's line denotes an inborn, untaught impulse given to the coffee-house wits by the goddess Criticism.

clue.text: Good friend of Sylvander Burns

parts.note: Robert Burns signed himself Sylvander in letters to Agnes McLehose, whom he addressed under a pastoral pen-name

explanation.surface: A dear friend of a man called Sylvander is on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns can look like a verb, but it is the poet Robert Burns, who used the name Sylvander in his correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes McLehose wrote to Robert Burns under this Arcadian pen-name while he signed himself Sylvander.

clue.text: Gold shown by vice ring to Illyrian duke

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a vice is a sin
a ring is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Gold and a vice ring are presented to a nobleman from Illyria.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic term for gold, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Illyria in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, who opens the play with 'If music be the food of love', bears this name.

clue.text: Godlike in terror ()

definitions.meaning: relating to the Greek woodland god Pan

explanation.surface: Something divine found within fear.
explanation.walkthrough: The rare adjective means 'of Pan'; sudden fear was blamed on Pan, giving the everyday word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes things belonging to the god Pan, and also sudden alarm, which the Greeks attributed to him.

clue.text: Ordinary boy with good example of Gregorian chant

parts.note: ordinary means plain
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An ordinary lad with a good voice sings Gregorian chant.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaccompanied single-line church music of the medieval kind, of which Gregorian chant is the principal tradition.

clue.text: Like Forster's transport

parts.note: E M Forster's short story features a heavenly bus, so the transport is described by the adjective in its title

explanation.surface: Resembling the vehicle a novelist travelled by.
explanation.walkthrough: Forster's story The Celestial Omnibus tells of a boy who rides a bus to a heavenly realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Forster's short story names its bus as heavenly, and the adjective means belonging to the sky or heaven.

clue.text: USA add the new name of St Jude

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of USA add the are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: America gives a saint a fresh name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges USAADDTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Jude is listed as Thaddaeus in the Gospels of Matthew and Mark, an alternative name for the same saint.

clue.text: Goethe's Goetz, never velvet-gloved

definitions.meaning: Goethe's play is Götz von Berlichingen mit der eisernen Hand, about a knight with an artificial metal fist
the proverbial firm rule is a hard fist in a soft glove; without the glove it is plain harshness

explanation.surface: A Goethe hero who never softened his grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Goethe's knight Götz wore a metal prosthetic fist, and the phrase also means ruthless control, the opposite of soft handling.

clue.text: Everyone adequate, according to Fielding squire

parts.note: everyone means all
worthy can mean good enough or deserving, adequate

explanation.surface: Everybody is good enough, says a novelist's landed gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Squire Allworthy is Tom's benevolent guardian in Henry Fielding's Tom Jones.
explanation.definitionFit: The kindly landowner who adopts the foundling hero in Henry Fielding's novel Tom Jones bears this name.

clue.text: Hero worship was the death of him

definitions.text: Hero worship was the death of him

parts.words: Hero worship was the death of him
parts.note: Hero is the priestess of the Greek legend, whose lover drowned swimming the Hellespont to reach her

explanation.surface: A man's adoration of an idol killed him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hero worship' reads as idolising a celebrity; here Hero is a woman's name, and love for her killed the swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the young lover swam the Hellespont nightly to visit Hero and drowned in a storm.

clue.text: Wilson's humanist seen on the beach

definitions.meaning: Bernard ..., the humanist novelist hero of Angus Wilson's Hemlock and After
grains of sand covering a shore

explanation.surface: A novelist's character spotted at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Angus Wilson's humanist writer is Bernard Sands, and beaches are covered in fine grains of crushed rock.

clue.text: His characters were ratbags

parts.note: Keith ... book Ratbags profiled Australian eccentrics, the characters of the title

explanation.surface: A writer whose characters were all scoundrels.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratbag is Australian slang for an eccentric or rogue; Keith Dunstan's 1979 book of that name profiled colourful Australian characters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian journalist Keith Dunstan wrote Ratbags, a book about real eccentric Australian personalities.

clue.text: Humorous writer reveals French ego adding capital

parts.note: je is French for I, the ego
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A comic author lets slip his French self while adding a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerome K Jerome wrote the comic Three Men in a Boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome K Jerome, author of Three Men in a Boat, is a celebrated comic novelist.

clue.text: Syrian soldier miraculously cured after consultation

definitions.text: Syrian soldier miraculously cured after consultation

parts.words: Syrian soldier miraculously cured after consultation
parts.note: in the Second Book of Kings a Syrian commander consults the prophet Elisha and is healed of leprosy

explanation.surface: A Syrian soldier recovers wondrously after seeing a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Elisha told the Syrian general to bathe seven times in the Jordan, and his leprosy was cured.
explanation.definitionFit: The Syrian army commander of 2 Kings 5 was cleansed of leprosy after seeking out the prophet Elisha.

clue.text: Shakespearean mistress taken too far?

definitions.meaning: Mistress ..., the bawd in Measure for Measure

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare woman went too far.
explanation.walkthrough: Mistress Overdone keeps a brothel in Shakespeare's Measure for Measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's brothel-keeper in Measure for Measure is Mistress Overdone, and the word also means exaggerated or overcooked.

clue.text: Candidate expects to take orders

parts.note: taking holy orders means becoming a priest; the candidate is one preparing for that

explanation.surface: A job applicant hopes to be told what to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take orders' suggests obeying a boss; in church use, taking orders is ordination.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in training for the priesthood, about to receive holy orders, is a candidate for ordination.

clue.text: Crécy girl, Saint-Loup's mother-in-law

definitions.meaning: ... de Crécy, the courtesan Swann loves in Proust
Saint-Loup marries Gilberte, the daughter of Swann and this woman

explanation.surface: A girl from a French town is related by marriage to a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Both definitions come from Proust's In Search of Lost Time; Crécy is her surname, not the battle site.
explanation.definitionFit: Proust's courtesan de Crécy marries Swann, and their daughter Gilberte weds Robert de Saint-Loup.

clue.text: Lawrentian fratricide and suicide

parts.note: in D H Lawrence's Women in Love ... Crich accidentally shot his brother as a boy and later walks to his death in the snow

explanation.surface: A Lawrence character killed his brother and then himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Gerald Crich of Women in Love killed his brother in a childhood shooting accident and dies in the Alpine snow.
explanation.definitionFit: D H Lawrence's mine-owner in Women in Love shot his brother as a child and dies in the Alps.

clue.text: Betjeman's was Calvinistic

parts.note: John Betjeman wrote a poem whose title pairs Calvinistic with a sunset church service

explanation.surface: A poet's church service was Calvinist.
explanation.walkthrough: Betjeman's poem is Calvinistic Evensong.
explanation.definitionFit: Betjeman's poem title names the Anglican service of sung evening prayer and calls it Calvinistic.
